why:
ours is `create_node(&mut self, name: &str) -> NodeHandle`, rclrs's is `create_node(&self, options) -> Arc<Node>`. Two differences, both structural: ours takes `&mut self` because the node is allocated in the executor's arena (static entity storage: the executor's entity table is an arena sized at compile time (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_HANDLES`) with no allocator behind it, and a `HandleId` is an index into it. Registration is one-way -- no slot is ever reclaimed and no handle is ever invalidated.), and it hands back a borrowing `NodeHandle` rather than an `Arc` -- no allocator, and RFC-0043/0044 make the Rust API a declarative component model where a user implements the `Node` trait rather than holding one. See `cpp:Executor::create_node`.

phase-427 W10 (2026-09-08) — DISPOSITION WRITTEN: `adopt`. The method itself is not new (phase-376 W5/B1 gave it the `(name, namespace)` dedup that makes it a registration rather than a handle factory); what W10 completed is the SEQUENCE it sits in. `Context::create_executor()` now opens the session with no name on it, so `executor.create_node("talker")` is where a node is named — the same name, the same position, the same one-per-distinct-name contract as upstream. Before it, a ported `create_node` call had a working method to land on but no `create_executor` above it, and the name was set on `ExecutorConfig::node_name` instead, which can only ever describe the FIRST of the several named nodes RFC-0047 puts in one image. That setter is deprecated for a release behind `nros-node/deprecate-node-name-setter` (feature-armed because this workspace sets `warnings = "deny"`, so an always-on attribute is 65 hard errors in unmigrated tests, benches, boards and examples rather than a nudge).

`adopt` rather than `adopt-bounded`: nothing about the CONTRACT is weakened. The two differences above are visible in the signature and the compiler names both — a ported `let node = ...` needs `mut` (rustc says so on the binding) and `Arc<Node>` is not what comes back (rustc says so at the first use). Neither silently does something else, which is the line RFC-0089 draws. Measured end to end in `packages/testing/nros-tests/tests/rclrs_talker_port.rs`: of the six lines that differ between the upstream tutorial and the port, `create_node`'s costs exactly the four characters of `mut`.
